content:
One way to finish this quest is to simply not do it. The quest can be completed if a player on the same team launches a nuke instead.

Once entering a silo bunker, be prepared for many robot enemies, mainly Mister Gutsies, Assaultrons, and Protectrons, with a few Eyebots and a Sentry Bot at certain points while navigating the silo in the tunnels and storage room. Eventually, the player will enter a high radiation zone in the silo's reactor chamber, which will linger until the reactor is shut down and fully repaired to prevent further radiation leakage.

Once having access to the silo's launch control center, and protecting the crew chiefs during launch prep from the security robots sent to stop the launch prep, enter a nuclear keycard into the marked terminal, the decrypted launch code in the terminal opposite, then use the main console between them to select the area to be struck by the nuke, confirm and watch the missile launch.

After gaining the rank of general and being appointed to the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Vault Dwellers need to head to the Whitespring Congressional Bunker command center. MODUS will proudly introduce the last section of the facility and invite player characters to familiarize themselves with the automated training for officers in charge of Appalachia's automated nuclear arsenal.

The quest requires Vault Dwellers to complete several steps. The tracking terminal at the command center allows them to trigger a surveillance sweep that will give them the rough location of either a code piece or a keycard convoy (starting the Hide and Seek and Destroy repeatable quest).

First, the codes. Each of the three silos (at Site Alpha, Site Bravo and Site Charlie) has its own individual launch code. These are gathered from ghoulified or Scorched officers with a field radio strapped to their back, easily identified by the chirping noise the radio pack makes when in range to hear it, and the blinking red light when close enough to see it. Killing them will yield a single letter/number pair necessary for decryption. The codes are automatically added at the command center and will display a seemingly random string of letters and numbers. Figuring out the word also produces the code for launching a nuke.

If Vault Dwellers want to ensure they have the correct code, they need to access the archival terminal in the command center armory and read Gen. Santiago's notes to learn about the Fujiniya Intelligence Base. Inside, they need to locate the lone terminal behind the blue fusion generators and use it to input the password from the bunker. This will produce a usable nuclear launch code.

Second, to input the code, Vault Dwellers require a nuclear keycard. These are ferried via automated cargobot convoys across Appalachia and collecting them is as simple as shooting down the cargobot, though taking out its vertibot escorts will make it easier as the vertibots shoot at anything they deem a threat to the cargobot, and damaging the cargobot's thrusters will render it unable to evade as easily while being fired on.

To launch a nuke, I'll need a Nuclear Keycard, a full set of silo Code Pieces, and information regarding the nature of the Code Pieces' encryption. MODUS' surveillance terminals can point me at the Code Pieces or a keycard. For the encryption, I can check the archives.
